verification_steps: Verify those destinations are persistent and included in a tested backup without deleting or pruning containers or volumes.
Confirm that the flow is linked to the expected existing config entry and integration identity.
Confirm service reachability and account status through a trusted official interface when an external outage is plausible.
Verify that the flow updates the existing entry rather than creating a duplicate identity.
After completion, verify entry reload and loaded state, representative entity updates, and a safe action.
Check the last successful automatic-backup timestamp and the current creation state, stage, and non-secret failure context.
Verify the expected artifact separately at every intended recovery location; do not infer integrity or restorability from discovery.

Confirm that the target is the official AdGuard Home integration and its applicable AdGuard Home server, not AdGuard public DNS, a browser/desktop product, another resolver, reverse proxy, host or container runtime.
Compare management reachability, current entity operation and management-reported DNS-server state without treating one as a proxy for another.
Verify DNS resolution and filtering behavior separately using a privacy-safe test; do not retain queried domains, client identity, addresses, logs, lists or rules.
Verify recovery on the same supported surface that failed; success on one surface does not prove all other surfaces healthy.
Confirm the expected artifact separately at each selected documented location; do not convert absence automatically into creation failure.
Confirm applicable storage availability without inventing a capacity threshold or attributing mount-point use to one workload.
Confirm the expected artifact is discoverable and the matching emergency kit or key is available, but never copy its contents into evidence or logs.
Verify that the documented current-system or onboarding workflow and available target storage apply to the installation method.
After a reported completion, check only the functions selected by the restore scope, including applicable Core, Supervisor, app, integration, storage, network, and radio boundaries.
Record pass, fail, partial, or not checked per recovery check; investigate failures independently and preserve evidence before retrying, deleting, resetting, or reinstalling.
Use only integration-documented recovery appropriate to the evidenced phase; do not delete the entry, edit storage, disable security checks, or repeat restart/reload as a generic first step.
Verify recovery by confirming the final lifecycle state and separately observing a fresh representative entity update and one safe supported action when applicable.
Confirm the configured DNS server is reachable.
Test required name resolution and response status behavior.
When filtering is involved, test the affected client resolver path separately from the server management API.
When discovery is involved, test unicast DNS separately from mDNS/DNS-SD and SSDP visibility.
Confirm whether ownership is user-managed Home Assistant Container, an external application, Home Assistant OS, or a Supervisor-managed App before selecting the diagnostic surface.
Compare configured resource boundaries and authoritative termination evidence before classifying resource pressure; do not infer out-of-memory termination from an ordinary exit.
Inspect only the least-sensitive relevant daemon, container stdout/stderr, health-check or application log surface and retain classifications rather than literal sensitive output.
Record parsing/validation, code-generation, compilation and artifact-production results separately without retaining YAML, secrets, paths, logs or firmware.
Verify API reachability, protocol/session and encryption compatibility separately without retaining endpoints, payloads or keys.
Verify discovery/manual setup, config-entry state, device connection and entity availability independently.
Check device power and network presence.
Verify host, native-API port, and encryption credentials without assuming firmware failure.
Verify source acquisition, detect-role and record-role behavior independently, and treat optional go2rtc/restream as its own layer when applicable.
Distinguish detector availability from motion, object analysis, tracking and review creation; do not classify absent activity as failure without a controlled expected test event.
Verify snapshots, recordings, media storage and database applicability independently; do not delete or recreate persistence as a generic first action.
Verify Frigate API separately from MQTT, then distinguish broker reachability, Frigate publication, Home Assistant consumption and entity/media representation.
Preserve evidence before restart or configuration changes, and verify recovery on the same supported surface without generalizing to the full pipeline.
For native Hue, verify discovery/manual host, bridge reachability, local API, authorization and config-entry state separately without retaining the host, bridge identifier or application key.
Compare bridge-wide evidence with bridge-reported child reachability and Home Assistant entity availability before selecting a bridge, Zigbee or physical-device branch.
For Hue Bridge Matter exposure, verify bridge capability, Matter commissioning/fabric and bridged exposure separately from underlying bridge Zigbee and native Hue API state.
Apply native Matter checks only when authoritative product evidence identifies a Matter-enabled Hue bulb and keep Thread Border Router and Matter fabric evidence separate.
Check bridge generation, product class and path-specific update applicability before considering an update; do not update speculatively.

Confirm that the target is the official Jellyfin integration and its configured Jellyfin Server, not a client, generic media player, DLNA, Cast, Kodi, Plex, Emby, Music Assistant, proxy, host/container or storage backend.
Compare integration update, entity availability, current session presence and playback category independently; treat no session or no active playback as neutral.
Verify recovery on the same supported surface that failed; avoid integration recreation, database deletion, library rebuild, container recreation or permission expansion as generic first actions.
Confirm the device actually supports Matter.
Verify the Matter integration and Matter Server connection.
For Thread devices, verify border router, credentials, IPv6, and phone proximity separately.
Test DNS only for a hostname, then route, RouterOS API service exposure, configured port and plain-versus-API-SSL mode as separate layers.
Apply only the identified recovery, then verify entry load, repeated fresh coordinator updates, entity availability and an independent safe router observation.
Confirm the configured broker endpoint and whether the broker is running.
Test name resolution and network reachability from the Home Assistant context.
Review authentication and TLS validation without disabling security as a first response.
Confirm the applicable broker listener and then evaluate DNS applicability, route, TCP and optional TLS independently.
Identify the selected Music Assistant Server deployment and verify runtime state separately from privacy-safe API connection outcome.
Verify each applicable provider path's local, cloud, account, storage, network and DNS dependencies from its current authoritative documentation.
Compare request, queue state, player acknowledgement, stream creation, stream delivery, reported playback and endpoint-level audible evidence separately.
Verify the Monitoring path, authentication and documented authorization scope separately; do not broaden access or disable TLS verification as a generic test.
Check configured background-job mode separately from attributable execution evidence; apply no invented freshness interval.
Verify API reachability separately from TLS trust, authentication and effective authorization; do not disable certificate verification or broaden privileges as a generic test.
Verify intended guest runtime state before treating stopped or suspended status as a fault, then use guest- or application-level evidence for workload health.
Preserve evidence before node reboot, guest restart, migration, storage or cluster change and verify recovery on the same attributable surface.
Compare phase-scoped connection outcome, generic entity availability, and directly observed supported privacy mode.
Verify current official product and feature applicability before treating a missing entity or media surface as a fault.
Preserve evidence before reconfiguration and verify recovery on the same supported surface that failed.
Verify the exact product category and whether Home Assistant should connect directly or through an NVR/Home Hub using current official information.
Confirm that device initialization is complete and that the supported device-local admin credential path—not a cloud account—is being used, without recording credentials.
Preserve evidence before reconfiguration and verify recovery with successful setup plus an initial supported state refresh.
For supported Gen1 only, verify the local HTTP request path separately from CoIoT enablement, peer mode, update delivery, freshness and any Repair issue.
For supported Gen2+ only, verify RPC channel, request, correlated result/error and component method separately from WebSocket establishment and notification delivery.
Compare device-wide evidence with the affected component, channel and entity before selecting a whole-device branch.
Verify authentication as its own phase and never log, export, reproduce or disable credentials.
Apply Bluetooth checks only to documented non-battery Gen2+ proxy behavior or an explicit BLU/BTHome/gateway path; do not infer Bluetooth control transport.
Apply Matter checks only after official product- and generation-specific evidence establishes native Matter applicability and then use the separate Matter integration boundary.
Compare installed firmware only with exact documented generation/product minimums and do not update speculatively.
Confirm official versus community/custom ownership and verify exact-device applicability using the authoritative project for that path.
Verify recovery on the same path and operation; explain possible identity, entity, automation and feature changes before any path migration.

Check whether the entity exists in the runtime state machine, whether its entity-registry entry is enabled, and whether that entry links to the expected config entry and device; do not edit registry storage.
Compare the backend entity state with the current frontend presentation; record a frontend-only divergence without treating UI or cache state as a root cause.
Test the actual service or device path with an integration-supported, non-destructive check where available; keep endpoint, service, device, and entity reachability conclusions separate.

Verify recovery independently by refreshing System Health, confirming the config-entry state, observing a fresh entity update, and testing one safe representative action where the entity supports control.
Compare the attributable authentication result, communication result, coordinator update-success context, and entity availability; do not derive one from another.
Verify the exact current supported model and feature boundary, including documented removed or limited entities, before treating absence as device failure.
Preserve evidence before reconfiguration and verify recovery with a successful update plus current behavior of the affected supported capability.
Confirm that the visible product belongs to the current official TP-Link Smart Home supported-device list and distinguish the Tapo virtual presentation from the tplink runtime.
Review only redacted integration diagnostics, remove credentials and identifiers, and verify recovery through config-entry loading plus an attributable device update.
Verify exact-device handler, converter, certification or project applicability using the authority for the selected path.
Verify recovery on the same path and phase; explain possible identity and feature discontinuity before any migration.
Test DNS only when a hostname is configured, then test routing, TCP reachability, TLS validation, API login, selected-site visibility, and WebSocket state as separate layers.
Compare controller availability with the affected managed device's power, address, VLAN, routing, inform, adoption, provisioning, and upgrade state.
Apply only the recovery documented for the identified layer, then verify config-entry load, WebSocket restoration, fresh events, entity availability, and an independent safe device observation.
Confirm that the target is the Protect application on a supported UniFi OS Console and not UniFi Network, Site Manager, ONVIF, Frigate, go2rtc, Reolink, or another integration.
Verify current official minimum Protect version, Stable-channel scope, category capability, and console-local user/API-key requirements without recording secret or identifying values.
Preserve evidence before reconfiguration and verify recovery on the same supported surface that failed.
Identify the selected deployment and verify process, application-startup and frontend states independently.
Verify coordinator hardware/firmware applicability, transport category and adapter-initialization result without retaining identifiers, paths, URLs or firmware versions.
Verify broker reachability, Zigbee2MQTT client connection and publication separately from Home Assistant MQTT connection, discovery processing and entity availability.
Verify coordinator and mesh conditions before removing or re-pairing devices.
Open the relevant retained trace and confirm whether the expected trigger appears.
If no trace is retained, verify YAML automation ID and trace-retention configuration before concluding that no run occurred.
Check whether the integration supports unload, reload, reconfigure, or reauth and use only the action matching the observed branch.
Verify the final config-entry state, expected entities, and a safe representative action after recovery.
Confirm whether the observation concerns config-entry first refresh or a later runtime update.
Compare the preserved exception with the integration-defined external dependency and test only that documented path using a non-destructive supported check.
Verify recovery with a later successful refresh and a representative fresh entity update before closing the incident.
Confirm that the issue is actionable and read its integration-specific explanation before changing configuration.
If a repair flow is offered, verify prerequisites and preserve a recoverable configuration or backup appropriate to the proposed change.
After the flow or manual fix, verify both the underlying behavior and issue deletion; do not treat either one alone as complete recovery.
Verify the next observable job completion state and named-layer evidence before treating a retry or recovery action as successful.
Record the relevant unsupported, unhealthy, issue, suggestion, and check entries with their non-secret type, context, reference, and identity fields.
Confirm the affected mount point and whether the high value persists.
Check free storage and backend reachability without deleting the database.
Confirm the selected local user has the required site and write permission and that the target device, port, firmware state, and action are supported.
Verify controller acknowledgement, fresh event state, port and PoE recovery, device reachability, downstream service recovery, and Home Assistant entity state independently.
Confirm the backup can be downloaded from its storage location.
Confirm matching encryption or emergency-kit material is preserved outside Home Assistant without exposing it.
Confirm the documented current-system or onboarding workflow, target storage, credentials, and selected content apply to the installation method.
After an actual restore, record installation-specific recovery checks separately from the restore result.
Grant the minimum role needed, verify expected entities, and tighten custom permissions where practical.
Verify that the recipient can diagnose with the reduced payload; provide additional data only when justified.
Compare growth with the configured retention period and purge behavior.
Check the Home Assistant client connection independently from device availability.
Add guards or redesign the feedback path after confirming causality.
Confirm whether the integration documents polling, push, or hybrid updates and record its supported or configured cadence without converting it into a universal threshold.
Check whether polling has active listeners, because the documented coordinator schedules periodic polling only while subscribed listeners exist.
Verify that a representative entity receives fresh source-backed data; an unchanged value can still be a successful update and must not be labeled stale solely because it did not change.
Confirm the configured database engine is supported.
Verify the database exists and the Home Assistant account has required permissions.
Test network and DNS paths separately from recorder configuration.
Verify active and inactive slot state, last-boot status, and installed version after the update attempt.
Compare the current feature with documented read, api and test policy requirements without recording account or network details.
Do not assign broad or full privileges merely to test a hypothesis.
After a bounded correction, verify the specific command, repeated polling and only the expected entity or tracker behavior.
Compare last-seen age with the configured detection interval and separate not_home from coordinator unavailable.
Verify client reachability or presence through an independent non-destructive observation without treating either as physical-location proof.
Change source or ARP options only for the evidenced failure branch, then verify across multiple polling intervals.
Compare free space with the current database size before starting maintenance.
Confirm the target is offered for the affected component.
Confirm Home Assistant knows the same network credentials.
Verify a usable border router and local IPv6 path.
Check roaming and delayed controller disconnect, the wired-client workaround, tracking options, multiple interfaces, and private or randomized MAC identity continuity.
Compare controller client state with a fresh network observation without treating either as proof of a person's physical location.
After a targeted change, verify a disconnect and reconnect cycle, fresh last-seen data, expiry behavior, and automation behavior separately.
Confirm the expected adapter identity and path.
